newsitem.title: UK: UK B/socs net new approvals s/a 3.434 bln in Feb.
newsitem.headline: UK B/socs net new approvals s/a 3.434 bln in Feb.

text.p: The UK Building Societies Association (BSA) released the following, seasonally adjusted, data on lending -
MORTGAGE ADVANCES AND NEW APPROVALS TO LEND (in 1000s)
NOTES - approval = borrower accepts offer of advance; advance = actual loan, on average some 10 wks after commitment; advances tend to reflect new approvals made 2 or 3 mths ago.
BSA director-general Adrian Coles said net and gross mortgage lending fell slightly on both a seasonally adjusted and unadjusted basis.
"However, the underlying trend is still upwards with approvals significantly higher than last month," he said.

"This slight downturn in lending should not be taken as an indication that the recovery in the housing market is faltering. The pattern in mortgage lending reflects the BSA view that a moderate recovery is continuing, despite some month on month fluctuations."
Some areas of the country were recovering very strongly indeed but others had still to see the full benefits of the upturn.
Building societies attracted an inflow of 1.551 billion stg in February, a 42 percent increase on January and the highest monthly figures since October 1988.

"Some of this big increase is undoubtedly a result of consumers topping up their accounts with converting societies. However, it is also likely that concern about the high price of equities and the highly competitive products and rates on offer at continuing building societies are further contributory factors."
